headword: {徳川家康|とくがわいえやす}
gloss: Tokugawa Ieyasu (1543-1616), founder of the Edo shogunate

definitions.gloss: Tokugawa Ieyasu, founder of the Edo shogunate
definitions.explanation: The warlord who unified Japan after the Sengoku period and founded the Tokugawa shogunate, which ruled for over 250 years until the Meiji Restoration. A central figure in Japanese history classes and period dramas.

examples.japanese: {徳川家康|とくがわいえやす}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{江戸幕府|えどばくふ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|ひら}いた→開く：01979_hiraku⟧。
examples.english: Tokugawa Ieyasu founded the Edo shogunate.

examples.japanese: {家康|いえやす}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{我慢強|がまんづよ}い→我慢強い：07164_gamanzuyoi⟧⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{知|し}られる→知る：00458_shiru⟧。

examples.english: Having won the Battle of Sekigahara, Tokugawa Ieyasu built the foundation for unifying the whole country.

notes:
Usually called simply {家康|いえやす} in casual reference. {徳川|とくがわ} is the family/clan name he founded a shogunate under; {家康|いえやす} the given name.

CULTURAL NOTE:
A famous saying attributed to him — "{鳴|な}かぬなら⟦{鳴|な}く→鳴く：04388_naku⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{待|ま}とう→待つ：00469_matsu⟧ホトトギス" ("If the cuckoo won't sing, wait until it does") — is used to contrast his patient temperament with the more impulsive ⟦{織田信長|おだのぶなが}→織田信長：30992_odanobunaga⟧ and ⟦{豊臣秀吉|とよとみひでよし}→豊臣秀吉：30993_toyotomihideyoshi⟧, his predecessors in the unification of Japan.
